Questions Before You Start

Do I need a real estate license? +
No license. No agent. No middleman. Tax deed auctions are run by county governments and open to any member of the public. You register, you bid, you win. The course shows you exactly how to do it from your computer, even if you've never set foot in the U.S.
Is this actually legal? +
Not only is it legal. It's government-run. When a property owner stops paying taxes, the county takes the property and sells it publicly to recover the debt. Every deed is recorded. Every transaction is verifiable. This market has existed for over a century. The only reason most people don't know about it is because nobody told them.
How much money do I need to get started? +
Less than you think. Some properties sell for a few thousand dollars. Others for tens of thousands. The Property Map inside this system is specifically designed to help you identify which ones are worth bidding on and which ones to skip. So you're not guessing with your money. You don't need to be rich to start. You need to know the criteria.
What if I don't want to deal with renovations? +
Then don't. Not every property needs renovation. Many are bought, titled, and resold without a single nail being hammered. And if you want something truly hands-off, the Invest-With-Me opportunity inside the members area lets you put up the capital while the entire operation is handled for you.
I'm not from the U.S. Can I still participate? +
Yes. The auctions are public, the records are online, and the entire process can be done remotely from anywhere in the world. You don't need to be physically present to research, bid, or close a deal. Everything you need to operate from your country is inside this lesson.
What if it's not for me? +
Then you pay nothing. You have 30 full days to go through the entire course, run the Property Map, watch the live auction recording, and decide. If at any point you feel this isn't right for you, send one message and you get a full refund. No forms. No explanations. No back and forth. The risk is entirely ours.
